app.name: Rikuri Node
cert.title: Let’s make this connection private
cert.lead: Your node made its own certificate. Install it once on this device and check it on the next page; then no one else on your network can read what you type here, like your password.
cert.installed_text: Continue on the private page. There you’ll check that it’s really your node before you type anything.
cert.stop: Not sure? You can stop here. Nothing on your node changes until you claim it.
steps.iphone.1: Tap Download the certificate, then Allow.
steps.iphone.2: Open Settings, tap Profile Downloaded, then Install.
steps.iphone.3: Go to Settings › General › About › Certificate Trust Settings and turn on Rikuri Node CA.
steps.android.2: Open Settings and search for “CA certificate”. Tap it, then Install anyway.
steps.android.3: Choose rikuri-node-ca.crt from your downloads. The menus’ names differ a little from phone to phone.
steps.mac.1: Click Download the certificate, then open rikuri-node-ca.crt from Downloads. Keychain Access opens.
steps.mac.2: Double-click Rikuri Node CA, open Trust, and set “When using this certificate” to Always Trust.
steps.mac.3: Close the window, and enter your Mac’s password to confirm.
steps.windows.1: Click Download the certificate, then open rikuri-node-ca.crt and choose Install Certificate.
steps.windows.2: Choose Current User, then “Place all certificates in the following store”, and pick Trusted Root Certification Authorities.
steps.windows.3: Click Finish, then Yes when Windows asks whether to install it.
steps.linux.2: In Firefox: Settings › Privacy & Security › Certificates › View Certificates › Authorities › Import, and tick “Trust this CA to identify websites”.
steps.linux.3: In Chrome or Chromium: Settings › Privacy and security › Security › Manage certificates › Authorities › Import.
secure.title: The connection is private
secure.lead: Your browser now trusts your node’s certificate. One last check makes sure it’s really your node, and not something pretending to be it.
secure.check1_after: . Its screen shows a fingerprint: two lines of letters and numbers.
secure.check2: Here, open the certificate behind the padlock beside the address, go to its chain (Details or Certificate Hierarchy), and pick the top one, Rikuri Node CA. Find its SHA-256 fingerprint.
secure.check3: They must match exactly. If they don’t, stop, and unplug the node’s network cable.
secure.check_iphone: On iPhone or iPad, Safari shows no certificate: open Settings › General › VPN & Device Management, tap Rikuri Node CA, then More Details, and find its SHA-256 fingerprint.
secure.check_android: On Android: open Settings and search for “Trusted credentials”. On its User tab, tap Rikuri Node CA and find its SHA-256 fingerprint.
secure.why: Why your device and not this page? A page can be copied by anyone. Only your device knows which certificate it really trusts.
secure.next: When the fingerprints match, claim the node with the code on its screen and choose your password.
claim.title: Claim your node
claim.lead: Whoever claims the node first becomes its owner. Use the code on the node’s screen, and choose the password you’ll sign in with.
claim.code_hint: At the node, press Ctrl+Alt+F2, then Enter. The code looks like K7QM-4XD9-TR.
claim.mismatch: The two passwords are not the same.
claim.tip: Tip: a few unrelated words, like “harbor violet tractor maple”, are long, and easy to remember.
claim.keep: Write it down or keep it in a password manager. Nothing can reset it yet: a way to reset it at the node comes with a later update.
claim.wrong_code: That code is not the one on the node’s screen. Check it and try again; a code can also expire, so press Enter at the node for a new one.
claim.already: This node already has an owner. Sign in with its password.
claim.policy: The node did not accept that password:
signin.title: Sign in to your node
signin.wrong: That password is not the node’s. Try again.
signin.unclaimed: This node has no owner yet. Claim it first.
home.title: This node is yours
home.until: You stay signed in on this device until {date}.
